Subject: Acme - context length & pricing follow-up

Hi Sam — great call this morning, thanks for walking through the integration and product goals. Quick recap and a few asks so we can run a concrete pricing exercise for your workload:

1) Confirmed goals:
- Primary: deploy assistant + summarization for enterprise users (end-user facing).
- Target unit economics: <= $15 / 1M tokens, ideal ~$10 / 1M (you mentioned)
- Must support occasional very long contexts for legal/claims review (possible 128k needs)

2) Items I need from you to finalize numbers:
- Typical request profile: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens (per request)
- Monthly token volume (prompt & completion split if available)
- Percent of requests that need >8k / >32k / >64k / >128k contexts
- Any peak QPS or concurrency targets

3) Next steps I will take once I have the numbers above:
- Produce a blended hosted vs dedicated cost estimate with unit economics (target $/1M tokens)
- Show how many tokens fall into 8k/32k/128k buckets and the cost delta for each
- Include recommended model/quantization profile and order-of-magnitude latency expectations

I attached the quick usage export template (acme-usage-export.csv) — if you can drop your monthly sample there and send back, I'll run the numbers and share a one-page proposal.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. See the numbers below and I attached our Q1 export (usage_report_q1.csv). Let me know if you want raw logs.

- Avg prompt tokens per request: 520
- Avg completion tokens per request: 1,350
- Monthly active requests: ~140,000 requests/month
- Monthly tokens (approx): 235M prompt tokens, 420M completion tokens (total ~655M tokens/month)
- Context-length distribution (requests): ~75% < 8k, ~20% 8k-32k, ~5% regularly hit >32k (we have a small set of long-document workflows that can require 128k sometimes)
- Peak concurrency: bursts to ~120 concurrent requests during business hours, sustained ~25-40 concurrent

Budget/targets:
- Procurement target: <= $15 / 1M tokens, ideally $10 / 1M blended
- Procurement contact: Elena S. (CC'd) — she handles commercial and PO process

Let me know if you need anything else and happy to hop on a quick follow-up.

Best,
Sam

Subject: Re: Acme - context length & pricing follow-up

Thanks Sam — this is perfect. I ran a quick blended estimate from Redwood based on your profile and a few assumptions; attaching the one-page proposal (redwood-proposal-acme-v1.pdf) for the detailed math, but summary below:

Assumptions used
- Avg tokens/request = prompt (520) + completion (1,350) = 1,870 tokens
- Monthly total tokens = ~655M (as you provided)
- Context bucketing: 75% under 8k, 20% 8k-32k, 5% >32k (inc. occasional 128k needs)
- Baseline hosted list blended price (without commitment) used for reference: $20 / 1M tokens for large-context models; Dedicated discounts applied in scenarios below

Scenarios (blended $/1M tokens, inclusive of prompt+completion usage):
1) Hosted pay-as-you-go (no commit) — blended estimate: ~$19.50 / 1M (higher due to long-context model usage)
2) Hybrid (hosted + model-variant routing for long docs) — blended estimate: ~$14.00 / 1M with a 6-12 month usage commitment and routing rules (route heavy long-context jobs to specialized nodes)
3) Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended for your volumes & predictability) — blended estimate: ~$10.75 / 1M with a 12-month reserved commit (includes higher throughput, lower tail latency, and quantization recommendations)

Example unit economics at your volumes (655M tokens / month):
- At $10.75 / 1M: monthly cost ~ $7,046 (655 * $10.75) -> note: this is in thousands format; detailed spreadsheet in the PDF shows model split and per-bucket cost
- At $14 / 1M: monthly cost ~ $9,170
- At $19.50 / 1M: monthly cost ~ $12,772

Notes on 8k/32k/128k impact:
- Most of your requests (75%) fit in 8k-friendly execution; those get best batching and lower per-token cost.
- The 20% at 8k-32k and 5% above introduce ~1.7-2.6x per-token cost due to increased memory and throughput constraints for long-context kernels; we model this in the proposal and show how routing + caching/KV strategies reduce the effective cost.

Recommended next steps:
- If procurement is comfortable with a target around $10-12 / 1M, we should scope a 12-month reserved capacity proposal and SOW.
- I can produce a 1-page SOW + pricing table that breaks out 8k/32k/128k per-token rates and expected monthly spend by bucket.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical + procurement sync — Wed Apr 7, 2027 at 10:00 AM PT. Does that work?

I attached the proposal PDF with the model-level math and a sample contract term sheet. Happy to walk through it on the call and revise to meet Elena's procurement needs.

—Marissa

- Procurement target: we can stretch to $12 / 1M with a 12-month commit and reasonable SLA.
- We're more interested in a Dedicated reserved capacity option given predictability and the long-context workloads; please include the dedicated node sizing in the SOW.
- Elena (CC) will own commercial terms and schedule a legal/procurement review. Elena — can you share your standard PO timeline?
- Confirming Wed Apr 7, 10:00 AM PT for the follow-up — I'll have Elena join as well.

Also can you share SOC2 + data residency notes before the meeting? Procurement will want those.

Appreciate it — talk tomorrow.

Best,
Sam
